lens_trajectory.note: lens trajectory (captions only, post-hoc): each arm's generated caption is teacher-forced onto its prompt (one extra forward per image per arm, no edits active) and the calibrated J-lens readout (x14's _calibrated_lens_logits: identity transport + bias, * scale, unembed, / temp, + logit_bias; unfitted layers read raw) is evaluated at the CAPTION token positions only: mean P(yes) = softmax probability of the x18 yes id, and object_in_top_k = the rate at which one of the image's annotated category emission ids (x14's ' '+name final-subword convention) is in the readout's top-k. shift_vs_baseline = arm mean - baseline mean per layer (same images, so the shift is paired)

notes.contrast: m3id/vcd contrast: the contrast prompt (the image-free text, or the image with distortion) is forwarded ONCE per sample and its FINAL-POSITION logits are reused as a per-step CONSTANT contrast vector: step_logits - tau * contrast. The contrast prompt tokenizes to a different sequence length than the image prompt (image placeholders), so per-step re-forwarding would need a per-step position alignment that does not exist; the constant vector makes the contrast EXACT at the prefill/handoff decision (generated token 0) and an approximation afterwards. Both arms share one LogitsProcessor; only the contrast vector differs
notes.vcd_form: vcd uses the m3id subtraction form logits - tau * logits_distorted (the x25 spec's 'same but' reading) rather than canonical VCD's (1+alpha)*l - alpha*l_aug, which differs by the +alpha*l term; the same tau grid as m3id is used so the contrast weight is directly comparable across arms
notes.distortion: vcd distortion is PIL-only (the repo invariant: images reach processors as PIL, no torchvision): RGB float array + seeded numpy gaussian noise (sigma on the 0-255 scale) clipped back to uint8, then PIL ImageFilter.GaussianBlur(radius). Seeded per sample (seed, sample index) so every arm sees the same distortion
notes.prior_ablate: prior-ablate direction: v_l = normalize(h_l(image) - h_l(no image)) measured at the FINAL PROMPT position of each prompt (the handoff position whose distribution predicts generated token 0; the x14 step_records[0] convention) in the RAW residual space at --ablate-layer. This is a measured state difference, NOT a token J-lens vector, so ResidualEditor's token-string resolution is bypassed (DirectionEditor) while its hook machinery and apply_edit ablate semantics are reused verbatim: h' = h - alpha * <h, v_l> v_l at the edited positions
notes.positions: the ablation scope is ResidualEdit positions='last': the prefill forward's final row (the handoff position) and every single-token decode row — the DECISION positions. Image-token rows are untouched (they do not recur under KV caching), so visual content keeps flowing while the image-prior component is removed where tokens are chosen (x23 SWAP_NOTE's text-scope decode convention)
notes.pope_parse: the answer is the LEADING yes/no token of the generated text: the first alphabetic word, lowercased, must be 'yes' or 'no' (tokenizer-agnostic string parse; 'Yes, there is...' -> yes, 'No.' -> no, anything else -> unparsed). Unparsed counts as INCORRECT for accuracy/F1 and is reported separately (it is a real failure mode, not a tie-break). Stricter than x18's parse_answer, which falls back to a unique yes/no anywhere in the text
notes.pope_slice: per-split records are the FIRST --n-images records of the shipped jsonl (POPE files are balanced by construction; the prefix slice keeps that balance and is deterministic)
notes.chair: CHAIR-s (sentence level) = fraction of captions mentioning >= 1 COCO category that is NOT annotated on the image; CHAIR-r (recall) = mean over images of |mentioned AND annotated| / |annotated| (images with an empty annotation set are excluded from the caption pool entirely, x23's convention). 'Mentioned' scans the caption for every category name in the instances file (the 80-class list — the standard CHAIR-in-COCO simplification)
notes.matcher: x25 in-arm matcher (the x25 spec's simple matcher; vlm_registry exposes no matcher to reuse): per category name, the case-insensitive word-boundary regex \b<name>(s|es)?\b — exact + plural-strip match. Documented gaps: no span masking ('hot dog' also matches 'dog'; the x13 matcher's span masking is the upgrade if CHAIR needs it), no irregular plurals ('mice' does not match 'mouse'), no synonym collapse
notes.trajectory: lens trajectory (captions only, post-hoc): each arm's generated caption is teacher-forced onto its prompt (one extra forward per image per arm, no edits active) and the calibrated J-lens readout (x14's _calibrated_lens_logits: identity transport + bias, * scale, unembed, / temp, + logit_bias; unfitted layers read raw) is evaluated at the CAPTION token positions only: mean P(yes) = softmax probability of the x18 yes id, and object_in_top_k = the rate at which one of the image's annotated category emission ids (x14's ' '+name final-subword convention) is in the readout's top-k. shift_vs_baseline = arm mean - baseline mean per layer (same images, so the shift is paired)
notes.synthetic: --synthetic builds the corpus in-memory (x23's exact convention): --n-images deterministic random RGB images, ids 1..n, each annotated with 2 categories cycled from the 16-name SYNTH_CATEGORIES pool. Synthetic POPE: 2 present + 2 absent questions per image per split ('Is there a <name> in the image?'), balanced 50/50; the absent pool is sampled uniformly regardless of split, so the popular/adversarial split NAMES exercise the per-split machinery but carry no hard-negative semantics (tiny has no real semantics)
notes.no_register_arm: arm 5 (register-off) is intentionally absent: T30 owns the visual-register arm
